One call on a published table: check, change, rates and trend

Source: R/tabrpt.R
tabrpt.Rd

The questions asked of a table an agency publishes are nearly always the same: are its categories sound, what changed from one period to the next and how sure can one be, what are the rates where there is a population, and does a short series trend. tabrpt() answers them in one call on a table in long form (one row per period and group), with the steps a reviewer needs and that are easy to forget on a deadline: exact intervals and p-values adjusted over every comparison, and the envelope that rounding in the release allows.

Usage

tabrpt(
  data,
  value,
  prd,
  by = NULL,
  pop = NULL,
  rnd = NULL,
  kind = "nearest",
  per = 1000,
  level = 0.95,
  adj = "BH",
  alpha = 0.05
)

# S3 method for class 'tabrpt'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

The table: a data frame in long form.

value

The column of the counts: one name.

prd

The column of the periods (numbers: a year, a month index): one name.

by

NULL, or the columns of the groups: names.

pop

NULL, or the column of the populations: one name.

rnd

NULL, or the rounding base of the published counts.

kind

"nearest" or "random" rounding.

per

The rates are given per per of pop: one positive number.

level

The confidence level of every interval.

adj

The adjustment of the p-values for the number of comparisons, as stats::p.adjust() names it.

alpha

The level at which an adjusted p-value is marked.

x

A tabrpt result.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class tabrpt, a list: check (the catchk() result, NULL without by), change (the yoypx() table), rates (the grprr() result, NULL without pop) and trend (a list of trndrr() results named by group, NULL for a group too short to test).

Details

The steps: catchk() on the group columns (with by); yoypx() on the counts by period within each group, with rnd, kind, level, adj and alpha; with pop, grprr() of the counts over the population pooled by group (by period when there is no by), per per; and for each group with three periods or more and a count above 0, trndrr() of its totals by period (over its population by period with pop). A group is the combination of its by columns, labelled with them joined by " / ". The refusals and warnings of the steps are given under the name tabrpt.

Examples

d <- data.frame(year = rep(2019:2023, 2),
                svc = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5),
                n = c(120, 131, 98, 105, 140, 30, 28, 41, 25, 33),
                pop = rep(c(50000, 12000), each = 5))
r <- tabrpt(d, "n", "year", by = "svc", pop = "pop", rnd = 5)
r
#> tabrpt: 10 group-periods, 8 changes tested, 0 marked after adjustment
#> groups: no problem found
#> rates per 1000: A 2.38, B 2.62
#> trend A: rate ratio per period 1.01, p 0.839
#> trend B: rate ratio per period 1.01, p 0.901
r$change[, c("group", "prd", "pctchg", "padj")]
#> yoypx: change on the earlier period
#>  group  prd     pctchg      padj
#>      A 2019         NA        NA
#>      A 2020   9.166667 0.7039955
#>      A 2021 -25.190840 0.1369352
#>      A 2022   7.142857 0.7700275
#>      A 2023  33.333333 0.1369352
#>      B 2019         NA        NA
#>      B 2020  -6.666667 0.8956832
#>      B 2021  46.428571 0.2960644
#>      B 2022 -39.024390 0.1707133
#>      B 2023  32.000000 0.5730293
